newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 1997 coconut exports seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 1997 coconut exports seen rebounding.

text.p: The Philippines, the world's largest exporter of coconut products, expects coconut production to recover in 1997 after a sharp fall last year and its exports to approach the all-time high of $1.1 billion.
The state-run Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) said it also expects prices to remain steady or rise because of growing demand in local and overseas markets.

PCA administrator Virgilio David said on Friday he expected the country's coconut crop to increase to 2.7 million tonnes. Production fell to an estimated 2.2 million tonnes in 1996 after it reached an all-time high of three million tonnes in 1995, he said.
David said the estimate of 2.2 million tonnes for 1996 was a revision of an earlier PCA forecast of 2.5 million tonnes.
A higher crop is expected this year because of relatively good weather in 1996. Last year's coconut production was hurt by a series of typhoons that struck growing areas in late 1995, David said.
Philippine coconut exports are forecast to reach between 1.6 to 1.7 million tonnes in copra terms this year.
"We may reach the all-time high level of $1.1 billion worth of coconut exports in 1997, similar to the figure in 1995, as prices are likely to stay at relatively high levels," David said.
Last year, the industry exported 1.457 million tonnes of coconut products worth $845.5 million, the second-highest export revenue in the past 15 years, he added.
Export volumes of coconut oil, which comprises the bulk of Philippine coconut sales, plunged 40.45 percent to 813,157 tonnes in 1996 from 1995's 1.365 million tonnes.

David said he expected the price of coconut oil to remain stable at its current $770 per tonne FOB or move even higher to the $800 per tonne level because of a steady rise in demand from oleochemicals firms and food processors.
Eighty percent of Philippine coconut exports go to Europe and the United States.
"Coconut oil commands a premium price compared to other vegetable oils because of its many uses," David said.

Data from the private trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines (UCAP) showed average monthly prices of the country's coconut oil exports hit $830 per tonne FOB in June 1996, the highest price since it fetched $839 in January 1985.

UCAP said it expects the country's coconut output to rise to 2.142 million tonnes this year from the 1996 forecast of 1.966 million tonnes. UCAP had also lowered its crop forecast in the past year from an earlier estimate of 2.334 million tonnes.

The PCA's crop estimate for this year was based on reports from coconut farmers about their expected harvests while the UCAP estimate was based on reports from farmers and traders, which may account for the discrepancies in the forecasts.

"Gauging from the rainfall pattern this year, it is anticipated that export volumes during the first semester next year would be bigger, representing 53 percent of the annual total, compared to the second semester," UCAP said.
David said the country's coconut harvest traditionally picks up in the second quarter of the year.

"If UCAP said they expect exports in the first half to be better than the second half, then they may know something we don't know, like some traders or farmers may still be holding some stocks from last year and are waiting for better prices," David said.
